item.title: Kenyan starvation cult leader convicted of deaths of nearly 200 children
item.description: Starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and 28 others were found guilty of murder by a Kenyan court on Monday over the deaths of 190 children and an adult in one of the world's worst cult-related tragedies in recent history.
item.dc:creator: Jefferson Kahinju
item.content:encoded: Starvation [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"cult leader Paul Mackenzie"] and 28 others were found guilty of murder by a Kenyan court on Monday over the deaths of 190 children and an adult in one of the world's worst cult-related tragedies in recent history. The preacher was [USN:L8N3Z51Y2 TEXT:"arrested in 2023"] after police received a tip-off, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola Forest near the coast in southeastern Kenya. Prosecutors say Mackenzie and his Good News International Church organised a Christian doomsday sect in which they ordered followers to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended. The case has gripped Kenya since the discovery of the mass graves. It raised questions over how Mackenzie was able to continue to operate despite having been on the radar of the authorities since 2017 when his premises were searched by police. In 2019, authorities shut down Mackenzie's church and he relocated to the Shakahola Forest, police said. GRANDFATHER HAILS JUDGMENT Mackenzie denied murder charges, saying he did not force the victims to starve, but the court rejected that argument. He and the others convicted will be sentenced on November 6. Defence lawyer Lawrence Obonyo, who represents Mackenzie and almost all of the others convicted, said he had been instructed to appeal. Francis Wanje, 62, lost eight family members including two grandchildren to the cult. He told Reuters that the judgment made him happy and gave him confidence in the judiciary. "So many are going to learn from what has come up today. ... You find churches everywhere, but they've got ill reasons for the churches. So it is good for members of the public to be very careful," Wanje added. HEARING LASTED MORE THAN EIGHT HOURS In total, more than 400 bodies have been recovered from the Shakahola Forest. Many of the children's bodies were severely decomposed, with only 26 able to be identified, and investigations into the other deaths are ongoing. Justice Diana Kavedza Mochache said in a hearing lasting more than eight hours that in some cases children were isolated and denied food while their parents watched. The director of public prosecutions, Renson Ingonga, told reporters afterwards at the Mombasa High Court: "That is the best judgment we would ever get." MACKENZIE SILENT WHEN JUDGE CALLED HIM BY NAME Mackenzie was in court, wearing a striped polo shirt and red trousers, sitting alongside his wife, one of the co-accused. When his name was read out by the judge he was silent, staring into space. The case has led to calls for tougher oversight of churches and other religious organisations in a country where religious faith plays a prominent role in public life. Kenyan President William Ruto said in 2023 that government agencies should have been able to prevent the deaths. He said he took responsibility as president. CHILDREN WERE FIRST TO STARVE People with direct knowledge of the cult's activities have [USN:L8N36W0BR TEXT:"told Reuters"] that Mackenzie planned the mass starvation in three phases: first children, then women and young men, and finally the remaining men. A former taxi driver, Mackenzie forbade cult members from sending their children to school and from going to hospital when they were ill, branding such institutions as satanic, relatives of some of his victims told Reuters for a 2023 article. Cult members lived in makeshift homes of polythene sheeting and thatch that Mackenzie divided into areas with biblical names like Jerusalem and Judea. The plight of his followers began to emerge in mid-March 2023, when a local man told police that his brother and wife had starved their children to death in the forest on Mackenzie's orders. Mackenzie was arrested but released on bail, after which relatives say he brought forward the date on which he told his followers the world would end. Police arrested him again in April 2023 and started combing through the forest more systematically and began exhuming mass graves. Mackenzie faces other charges over the forest deaths including terrorism-related ones, which he has denied. Prosecutors say while he was in detention he also directed the deaths of 52 people in [USN:L8N3Z51Y2 TEXT:"Kwa Binzaro village"], which lies about 30 km (18 miles) from Shakahola. Mackenzie has pleaded not guilty in that case.

item.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts has blood clots in lungs, out for season
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the season after further testing revealed blood clots in his lungs, the team announced Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the season after further testing revealed blood clots in his lungs, the team announced Monday. Hurts' condition is considered stable and he "has no significant functional limitations," the team said. His treatment for a new diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli will involve blood thinners, during which time he is unable to participate in contact activities. The 28-year-old veteran's prognosis is good and the team said it expects a full recovery with no long-term effects. Specialists in London initially diagnosed a superficial blood clot in Hurts' left calf on Oct. 10, the day before Philadelphia's 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Further testing discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs. "We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners," the team's statement concluded. "In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects." Regarding the decision to play Hurts in London, even though they reportedly were aware of the blood clot before the game. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said Monday regarding that decision, "(I) leave that up to the medical experts, but we always, always care deeply about our players. And that's when you are completely focused on together and connection. You're always thinking about the well-being of your guys and that's what we were in that situation. ... "I'm not a medical expert. I lean on our guys in all those situations, right? I'm a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them." Sirianni declined to reveal the substance of his latest conversation with Hurts after learning that the QB was out for the year, though he did say, "I just deeply care about him and hope that he continues to improve with what he's going through." Hurts, a three-time Pro Bowl selection and the MVP of Super Bowl LIX, has compiled a 59-28 regular-season record since taking over as the starter late in his rookie season in 2020. He has passed for 18,824 yards with 118 touchdowns and 48 interceptions and rushed for 3,661 yards and 64 touchdowns. Hurts completed 57.8% of his passes for 933 yards, eight TDs and three interceptions in five starts (2-3 record) this season. Backup Tanner McKee started in Hurts' place on Sunday as the Eagles (2-4) sustained their fourth consecutive loss, a 25-14 setback at home to the Carolina Panthers. "I have the utmost confidence in Tanner," Sirianni said Monday. --Field Level Media

item.title: 米住宅建設業者指数、10月は約14年半ぶり低水準 ローン金利・建材高が重し
item.description: [ワシントン １９日 ロイター] - 全米住宅建設業協会（ＮＡＨＢ）が１９日発表した１０月のＮＡＨＢ／ウェルズ・ファーゴ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米住宅建設業者指数、10月は約14年半ぶり低水準　ローン金利・建材高が重し 10/19 23:47 配信

米カリフォルニア州エンシニタスにある一戸建て住宅。８月撮影。REUTERS/Mike Blake

[ワシントン １９日 ロイター] - 全米住宅建設業協会（ＮＡＨＢ）が１９日発表した１０月のＮＡＨＢ／ウェルズ・ファーゴ住宅建設業者指数は２９と、前月の３２から低下し、２０１２年６月以来、約１４年半ぶりの低水準となった。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は３１への低下だった。

中東紛争により住宅ローン金利とエネルギー関連の建材価格が上昇しているほか、移民取り締まりに伴う人手不足や、関税措置によるコスト上昇が影響している。

住宅ローン金利はここ数週間で急上昇しており、住宅金融公社フレディマックのデータによると、３０年固定住宅ローン金利は先週、７．４０％と約３年ぶりの高水準となった。米国とイスラエルの対イラン戦争がインフレをあおる中、米国債利回りに連動して借り入れコストが上昇し、住宅販売を圧迫している。

ＮＡＨＢのビル・オーウェンズ会長は「住宅建設業者は、建設ローンや建築建材、ディーゼル燃料のコスト上昇に加え、慢性的な人手不足にも直面している」と指摘。「全米で建設業者の３分の１超が、過去１カ月間に自社の事業地域で移民取り締まりの動きがあったと報告しており、これが建設の遅れや、合法的な労働者が出勤を躊躇（ちゅうちょ）する事態を招いている」と述べた。

買い手を呼び込むために値下げを実施した建設業者は４３％と、２０─２６年の期間で最も高い割合となった。平均値下げ幅は６％と横ばいだった。販売促進策の実施率は６５％。１９カ月連続で６０％以上となっている。

現在の販売状況を示す指数は２ポイント低下の３３。販売見通しを示す指数は５ポイント低下の３２となった。

見込み客の来場状況を示す指数は５ポイント低下の１８。ＮＡＨＢのチーフエコノミスト、ロバート・ディーツ氏は同指数について、コロナ禍の２０年４月を除くと、１２年４月以来の低水準だと指摘した。

item.title: 米国株式市場・午前＝Ｓ＆Ｐ・ナスダック上昇、ＡＩ関連が反発
item.description: ［ニューヨーク １９日 ロイター］ - １９日午前の米国株式市場では、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合が上昇した。人...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場・午前＝Ｓ＆Ｐ・ナスダック上昇、ＡＩ関連が反発 10/19 23:33 配信

2026年7月20日に撮影 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

［ニューヨーク　１９日　ロイター］ - １９日午前の米国株式市場では、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合が上昇した。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株が前週の急落から反発したほか、原油価格の下落も支援材料となった。ナスダック総合指数は一時２５５．３ポイント（０．９８％）上昇した。

人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービスを手がけるコアウィーブは、投資判断の引き上げを受けて３．４％高と急伸した。

ゴールドマン・サックスは、同社の投資判断を「中立」から「買い」に引き上げた。コンピューティング能力の供給が逼迫していることや、競合企業に対する業績面での優位性から、今後２年間でメガワット当たりの年間経常収益が押し上げられるはずだとし、直近の下落は買いの好機だとした。前週には、同社の抱える５００億ドルの債務を巡る懸念がＡＩセクター全体に広がり、株価の４分の１超を失っていた。

競合のネビウス・グループは４．５％高。過去２週間で３１％超下落していた。データセンター運営のアプライド・デジタルは９％、ＩＲＥＮは５．７％、それぞれ上昇した。

フィラデルフィア半導体指数は２．８％高で推移。前週に１１％超下落し、ＡＩ関連の急落局面で最も打撃を受けた銘柄群の一つとなった。

インテルは５．６％上昇した。ＪＰモルガンが投資判断を「アンダーウエート」から「ニュートラル」に引き上げたことが材料となった。

エヌビディアは０．６％、ＡＭＤは４．３％、ブロードコムは２．２％、それぞれ上昇した。３社とも前週に大きく売られていた。

マイクロン・テクノロジーは３．８％高。前週には約１５％下落していた。データストレージのサンディスク、ウエスタン・デジタル、シーゲイトも前週の大幅安から反発した。

item.title: India probing Pernod, Diageo Scotch imports under India-UK trade pact, sources say
item.description: Indian tax officials are investigating whether liquor giants Pernod Ricard and Diageo wrongly classified some bulk Scotch imports, allowing them to pay lower tariffs introduced under the recently agreed India-UK trade pact, five industry sources familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Kalra
item.content:encoded: Indian tax officials are investigating whether liquor giants Pernod Ricard (PERP.PA) and Diageo (DGE.L) wrongly classified some bulk Scotch imports, allowing them to pay lower tariffs introduced under the recently agreed India-UK trade pact, five industry sources familiar with the matter said. Import tariff disputes have long been a [USN:L4N3P10W5 TEXT:"sore point"] for foreign investors in India and embroiled companies like [USN:L4N45E0CD TEXT:"Samsung"], LG and Volkswagen. They often involve large back-tax demands raised years after the items were imported, with Indian officials saying they are only enforcing the law. Last week, tax inspectors made an unexpected visit to Pernod's India headquarters near New Delhi where they questioned company executives about their Scotch imports, three of the people said. Diageo's Indian unit, United Spirits (UNSP.NS) , in a stock exchange filing last week said its offices in multiple locations were searched on Friday as part of an "industry-wide exercise" by authorities, without saying what the search related to. The other two people said Diageo is also being investigated for how it classifies some Scotch imports. Pernod (PERP.PA) told Reuters in a statement that it is cooperating with the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and providing all information requested, adding it was committed to addressing any questions from the authorities. Diageo (DGE.L) , also in a statement, said it is cooperating with Indian authorities, and has always complied with local laws. In its stock exchange disclosure, it said it had provided all documents and clarifications. The Indian revenue directorate did not respond to a request for comment. Reuters is first to report that tax inspectors visited Pernod's India office, and publish details of the probe, including that it is linked to the UK-India tariff declarations. BULK SCOTCH IMPORTS Diageo and France's Pernod Ricard dominate India’s $65 billion alcohol market. Both companies import bulk Scotch concentrates in containers to mix with other ingredients to make brands like Royal Stag, Blenders Pride and McDowell’s. Under the [USN:L4N43H0E5 TEXT:"trade pact"], which took effect on July 15, India agreed to slash import taxes on certain Scotch imports to 75%, from 150%. The tax inspectors argued that the duty relief did not apply to bulk concentrates, four of the people said. "The tax department is concerned that bulk imports are being wrongly classified," one of them said. ICONIC PRODUCT The UK accounts for almost 75% of India's imported spirits market, primarily driven by Scotch whisky, Crisil Ratings said this year. In July, the British government said "iconic UK products" including whiskies and gin would benefit from India's tariff changes. It added that the UK's whisky exports to the country were worth more than £200 million in 2022. Pernod is already facing antitrust cases in India, its biggest market by volume, and a [USN:L4N41Z12U TEXT:"$314 million"] back-tax demand for allegedly undervaluing some imports. The company denies wrongdoing. Diageo in August agreed to [USN:L4N44E10L TEXT:"reformulate"] some of its most popular drinks after the country's food safety regulator banned them in some states for adding flavours against regulations. During the visit to Pernod's India office on Thursday, tax inspectors reviewed some documents related to bulk Scotch imports, but have not been in contact since, said one of the people.

item.title: Qatari electricity lifeline for Lebanon includes two power plants, LNG supply deal
item.description: Qatar plans to construct two power plants in Lebanon over the next three years and sign a 20-year liquefied natural gas supply deal under a proposal to revive the ailing Lebanese power sector, a document seen by Reuters showed.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: Qatar plans to construct two power plants in Lebanon over the next three years and sign a 20-year liquefied natural gas supply deal under a proposal to revive the ailing Lebanese power sector, a document seen by Reuters showed. Lebanon's energy sector is at the centre of the country's financial and economic malaise, contributing tens of billions of dollars to the national debt since the country's 1975-1990 civil war even as it failed to deliver 24/7 power. The state power company currently supplies just a few hours of power per day, with the rest coming from expensive private diesel generators that spew toxic exhaust often seen forming a yellow-grey layer of smog above Beirut. Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al-Thani visited Lebanon last week and publicly promised to help revitalise the country's power sector. Few details were then presented to reporters. But according to a proposal drafted with input from the Lebanese and Qatari governments, dated October 2026 and seen by Reuters, the programme "covers gas-fired power generation, LNG supply and regasification, renewable energy, battery storage, and regional electricity interconnections". "The program aims to attract private/project financing without upfront Lebanese public-budget capital expenditure; payment obligations and guarantees remain subject to negotiation," the document said. The blueprint, named the National Integrated Energy Investment Program, still requires the approval of both governments and is subject to amendment, a person familiar with the matter said. They put the timeframe for implementation at three years if approvals come swiftly. Qatar has been a longtime financial and political backer of Lebanon, stepping in multiple times over the last decades during times of political and economic crisis. The Qatari Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the proposed plan. Lebanon's energy minister also did not respond to a request for comment. PROPOSAL FOLLOWS GROWING QATARI PRESENCE IN SYRIA According to the document, the plan includes two new combined-cycle plants at Deir Ammar in northern Lebanon and at Zahrani in the south, each at a capacity of 825 megawatts. QatarEnergy would also enter a 20-year LNG supply agreement with Lebanon, using both a floating storage and regasification unit with a capacity of 3.5 million cubic meters per day, and the Arab Gas Pipeline via Syria at a capacity of 4.5 million cubic meters per day. The proposal also includes plans for 800 MW of solar and 440 MW of wind, battery capacity and power imports from Syria, beginning with 300 MW via two separate routes. Numerous proposals to reform Lebanon's power sector and provide electricity through the national grid have repeatedly stalled due to political bickering and the vested interests of senior politicians in the fuel and energy sectors. The proposal would build on a growing Qatari presence in neighbouring Syria, where Qatari conglomerate Power International Holding has secured contracts for 5,000 MW of power generation, as well as oil and gas extraction and pipelines.

item.title: US Supreme Court will not review Trump's firing of labor board member
item.description: The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by a Democratic-appointed member of the National Labor Relations Board to challenge the legality of her firing by President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: John Kruzel
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by a Democratic-appointed member of the National Labor Relations Board to challenge the legality of her firing by President Donald Trump . The justices turned away former NLRB member Gwynne Wilcox's appeal of a lower court's ruling that said the Republican president's January 2025 firing of her was a valid exercise of executive authority. The court's action follows its June decision [USN:S0N3YR013 TEXT:"backing Trump's firing"] of Rebecca Slaughter, a Democratic Federal Trade Commission member. That ruling overturned the court's 1935 precedent in a case called Humphrey's Executor that had recognized the authority of Congress to protect leaders of certain regulatory agencies from presidential removal at will. The Slaughter decision capped a decades-long conservative push to strengthen the president's grip on key levers of government power. Trump's move to oust Wilcox from the NLRB was part of his shakeup and downsizing of the US government, including firing thousands of workers, dismantling federal agencies, installing loyalists in key jobs and purging career officials. "I'm disappointed that the Supreme Court has declined to hear this case, not only for myself, but also for the workers and employers who rely on the National Labor Relations Board to resolve labor disputes impartially and free from political pressure," Wilcox said in a statement. Wilcox added that she would remain committed to "protecting the principles that allow the board to serve the public fairly." The Justice Department declined to comment. Wilcox, the first Black woman to serve on the agency's board, was appointed to a second five-year term in 2023 by Democratic former President Joe Biden. Trump moved to fire her about a week into his second presidential term, drawing a lawsuit by Wilcox. Slaughter also was a Biden appointee. The legal fight over Trump's firing of Wilcox and other officials has figured as a key test of his efforts to bring federal agencies meant by Congress to be independent from the president under his control. US District Judge Beryl Howell in March 2025 upheld a federal law protecting NLRB officials from being fired without cause, rejecting Trump's argument that the measure passed by Congress encroaches on authority granted to the president under the US Constitution. That ruling was reversed in a 2-1 decision by the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit in December 2025, prompting Wilcox's appeal to the Supreme Court.

item.title: ジャカルタ株が過去2日で最大の下落、ＭＳＣＩに説明要求 市場改革も表明
item.description:
Ankur Banerjee Stefanno Sulaiman
[シンガポール／ジャカルタ １９日 ロイター] - ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ジャカルタ株が過去2日で最大の下落、ＭＳＣＩに説明要求　市場改革も表明 10/19 22:13 配信

株価ボード、ジャカルタのインドネシア証券取引所で16日撮影 REUTERS/Ajeng Dinar Ulfiana/File Photo

Ankur Banerjee　Stefanno Sulaiman

[シンガポール／ジャカルタ １９日 ロイター] - インドネシア株式市場は１９日、２営業日の下落としては過去最大を記録した。指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩが１６日、２０２７年に同国を「新興国市場」から除外する可能性を警告したことが売りを誘発。当局はＭＳＣＩに説明を求めた。

ジャカルタ総合指数は１６日に１１．６％急落したのに続き、１９日は３．６％安で取引を終えた。２営業日の下落率は１９９８年のアジア金融危機時を含め過去最大となった。取引時間中には６年ぶりの安値も付けた。

ＭＳＣＩが１６日、インドネシアを「新興国市場」から「スタンドアローン市場」に変更することを検討していると表明したことで売りが始まった。想定以上に厳しい分類変更の可能性に、投資家や当局者に動揺が広がった。

スタンドアローン市場に変更されれば、東南アジア最大の経済規模を持つインドネシアは国際資本へのアクセスを失い、投資先として周縁に追いやられる恐れがある。

不安心理からの売りは通貨や債券市場にも波及した。ルピアは１ドル＝１万８０３０ルピアに下落、６月に付けた過去最安値の１万８１９０ルピアに迫った。国債も下落し、１０年債利回りは１６日の７．１６９％から７．４％に上昇した。

インドネシア証券取引所のジェフリー・ヘンドリック最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、説明を求めるためのＭＳＣＩとの会合を前に「（ＭＳＣＩから）このような発表があるとは予想していなかった。予想外の声明で市場はパニックに陥った」と述べた。

＜資本市場改革への取り組み継続＞

ヘンドリック氏はＭＳＣＩとのオンライン会合後、１月にＭＳＣＩが最初の警告を発したことを受けて着手した資本市場改革に引き続き取り組むと述べた。会合の詳細は明らかにできないとした。

同氏はまた、市場の透明性と価格発見機能を改善するための２つの施策を発表した。同一の個人や法人に株式保有が高度に集中している銘柄をジャカルタ総合指数から除外する措置が含まれる。「主要指数の動きをより正確に示す」ことが狙いという。

インドネシア証券取引所（ＩＤＸ）は１９日、価格変動の抑制に向け、株価の１日の下落率の上限を１５％から７％に縮小した。それを下回る価格での売り注文を自動的に拒否し、一段の下落を防ぐ。

＜投資家、インドネシア資産への投資を再評価＞

ＭＳＣＩの動きを受け、投資家がインドネシア資産全般への投資を見直す中、規制当局や財政・金融当局への圧力が強まっている。

かつて新興国市場の有望な投資先だった同国からの資本逃避リスクへの懸念も高まった。投資家によると、新型コロナウイルスのパンデミック以降、プラボウォ大統領の下で財政の健全性や中央銀行の独立性への信頼が薄れる中、同国の魅力は既に低下していた。

事情に詳しい政府当局者２人によると、プラボウォ氏は１９日、財政・金融当局者と会合を開き、「現在の経済情勢」について協議した。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバル・レーティングのソブリン担当アナリスト、レイン・リン氏は、ＭＳＣＩの最新の警告で追加の資本流出が起きる可能性が高いものの、資金調達コストを大幅に押し上げる規模にはならないとの見方を示した。「より懸念されるのは、投資家の信頼が損なわれる可能性と、国債市場や海外直接投資にも投資家心理の悪化が広く波及するリスクだ」と述べた。

ゴールドマン・サックスは、ＭＳＣＩ指数から完全に除外されれば、パッシブ運用資金が５６億ドル流出する可能性があると推計。これらの指数をベンチマークとするアクティブ運用ファンドの保有額は８０億ドルを超えるものの、売却するかどうかは指数への連動ではなく、運用者の裁量によると記した。

海外投資家は２６年に入り、インドネシア株を４９億８０００万ドル売り越している。年間の資金流出額は少なくとも過去１６年で最大となるペースだ。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：北朝鮮が韓国と対立姿勢、米国にとって新たな悩みの種に 焦点：新興国投資ラッシュに取り残されるインドネシア、強い政策への不信感 アングル：スマトラ島豪雨被害、森林破壊で被害拡大か　地元に怒りの声 アングル：石炭依存の東南アジア、長期電力購入契約がエネ移行の妨げに 最終更新: 10/19(月) 22:13 ロイター

item.title: Germany's Merck buys Silence Therapeutics in $1.3 billion RNA drug deal
item.description: German drugmaker Merck KGaA said on Monday it would acquire UK-based Silence Therapeutics in an all-cash deal for about $1.3 billion, bolstering its pipeline of precision medicines and adding RNA-targeting drug technology.
item.dc:creator: Christy Santhosh
item.content:encoded: German drugmaker Merck KGaA (MRCG.DE) said on Monday it would acquire UK-based Silence Therapeutics in an all-cash deal for about $1.3 billion, bolstering its pipeline of precision medicines and adding RNA-targeting drug technology. Merck will pay $20 per American depositary share for Silence, representing a premium of 130% to the stock's last close. US-listed shares of Silence more than doubled in morning trading. The deal broadens Merck's gene-silencing capabilities by adding Silence's siRNA medicines, which work by switching off disease-related gene messages before they can produce harmful proteins. RNA, or ribonucleic acid, is a molecule that carries genetic instructions and helps tell cells which proteins to make. This is Merck's third major acquisition in less than two years, following its $3.9 billion purchase of SpringWorks Therapeutics in 2025 and its pending $11.3 billion takeover of life-sciences tools maker [USN:L8N42X0VJ TEXT:"Bio-Techne"]. Silence's lead therapy candidate, divesiran, is expected to enter late-stage testing for phlebotomy-dependent polycythemia vera, or PV, a rare blood cancer in which the bone marrow produces too many red blood cells. Patients with this condition require regular therapeutic blood draws, known as phlebotomies, to manage their red blood cell levels. With an approval, the drug would compete with Takeda (4502.T) and Protagonist's (PTGX.O) rival drug, Mimrylo. "With Takeda implying $1 billion to $2 billion in peak sales for Mimrylo in PV, the deal valuation does appear inexpensive considering Merck KGaA also gets the broader mRNAi GOLD siRNA platform as well," said William Blair analyst Myles Minter. Minter said the deal "takes the execution risk off the table in an increasingly competitive space". Silence is also developing zerlasiran for people with high lipoprotein(a), a blood protein linked to heart disease, along with earlier-stage treatments for high cholesterol, obesity and immune-related diseases. The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. The companies said the transaction will be effected through a UK scheme of arrangement.

item.title: Trump geothermal lease sale collides with planned Nevada solar farms
item.description: The US Interior Department's sale of geothermal leases in Nevada this week will include thousands of acres overlapping major planned solar projects fromNextEra Energy and other developers, according to federal documents.
item.dc:creator: Nichola Groom
item.content:encoded: The US Interior Department's sale of geothermal leases in Nevada this week will include thousands of acres overlapping major planned solar projects from NextEra Energy (NEE.N) and other developers, according to federal documents. On Tuesday, the Interior Department's Bureau of Land Management is scheduled to auction 83 parcels totaling 265,691 acres to geothermal developers. NextEra, the world's largest owner of solar and wind generation, asked the agency earlier this year to "remove, defer or reconfigure" three proposed geothermal parcels. President Donald Trump's administration has [USN:S0N3RO0B5 TEXT:"promoted"] geothermal energy as a source of always-on electricity while largely [USN:L1N3X1119 TEXT:"excluding"] wind and solar from a broad effort to accelerate federal permitting. In comments submitted to the agency during review of the sale, NextEra said the parcels in question overlap roughly 6,000 acres, or about 60%, of its planned 1,000-megawatt Sawtooth Energy Center in Nye County, Nevada. BLM declined NextEra's request in August, saying federal lands are managed for multiple uses. Maps published on the BLM website in August show overlaps involving six proposed geothermal parcels and four major planned solar developments in the Nevada desert. One parcel, which overlaps entirely with NextEra's Sawtooth project, did not appear on the auction website and appeared to have been recently removed from the sale. NextEra, based in Juno Beach, Florida, said in its comments that the overlap could "create a foreseeable conflict" with its pending application. "NextEra must collaborate with any potential lessee and adjust its operations accordingly to avoid land use conflicts," the agency said. BLM added that if NextEra's project is approved first, it would have the "senior right" and a geothermal development would have to avoid impacts on its project. Another solar developer, Dallas-based Leeward Renewable Energy, said a geothermal parcel overlaps about 735 acres of its proposed Lone Mountain solar project in Esmeralda County. It urged the agency to recognize the overlap "and the non-exclusive nature of any future geothermal lessee's development rights." The agency added a description and maps of the overlapping projects to its sale documents. They include the proposed 300-MW Nivloc solar project being developed by Invenergy and Arevia Power's 1,500-MW Gold Dust solar project. Along with Lone Mountain, those projects were part of the Esmeralda 7 development, a proposed complex of seven solar farms on 62,000 acres. BLM canceled the environmental review for the complex in 2025 but said the projects may reapply for federal approval individually. NextEra, Leeward and BLM did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

item.title: 中国人民銀、翌日物リバースレポ金利を主要政策金利に検討中
item.description: [北京／上海 １９日 ロイター] - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）が、主要政策金利を翌日物リバースレポ金利に切り替えることを...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国人民銀、翌日物リバースレポ金利を主要政策金利に検討中 10/19 19:40 配信

北京の中国人民銀行本部、2025年5月撮影 REUTERS/Tingshu Wang

[北京／上海 １９日 ロイター] - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）が、主要政策金利を翌日物リバースレポ金利に切り替えることを検討している。国営メディアが１９日に報じた。金融政策の伝達メカニズムを改善し、経済を下支えすることを目的とした方針転換となる。

中国では２０２４年以来、７日物リバースレポ金利が主要政策金利として機能してきた。

人民銀が運営する「金融新聞」によると、人民銀の潘功勝総裁は、この主要政策金利の変更は人民銀による短期金利のコントロール精度を高める取り組みの一環だとした。

同紙によると、北京で開催された主要な金融フォーラムで、潘氏は「現在、銀行間翌日物レポ金利は事実上、人民銀の金融政策における目標金利となっている」と発言。「この金利は短期流動性の需給を敏感に反映しており、近年はより高い安定性を示している」と語り、翌日物金利を主要金利とすることで金利管理がより精密になるとした。

この政策転換により、人民銀は流動性状況をより的確にコントロールできるようになり、その政策枠組みは世界の他の中央銀行とより整合性を持つようになる。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）などの中央銀行は、イールドカーブをより確実に定着させるため、すでに翌日物金利を主要な政策金利として採用している。

発表後、中国の３０年物国債利回りは１ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）以上低下した。

国泰君安国際のチーフエコノミスト、周浩氏は「金融政策の枠組みが海外と整合することになり、人民元の国際化を推進する上でよりスムーズになるだろう」と述べた。

金融情報サービス大手の中誠信国際のチーフマクロアナリスト、王青氏は、翌日物リバースレポの実際の運用金利は人民銀が切り替えを行う際に発表されるとし、今回の変更は利下げに相当するものではないと指摘した。

中国のインターバンク市場は潤沢な資金供給が続いている。翌日物レポ金利の平均は約１．２５％と約５カ月ぶりの低水準付近にあり、人民銀の翌日物リバースレポ操作における借入コストとして報じられている水準にほぼ沿っている。これは、現在１．４％となっている７日物リバースレポ金利を下回っている。

今回の変更は中国の金融構造の変化とも整合する。中国では、債券や株式を通じた直接金融が従来型の銀行融資を上回り、新規資金調達の主要な供給源となりつつあり、与信配分も不動産など与信依存度の高いセクターから徐々に離れつつある。

翌日物リバースレポ操作は、人民銀の政策手段に加わった最新のツールとして６月下旬に導入された。

翌日物取引は中国のインターバンク短期金融市場におけるレポ取引高の８割超を占めている。

潘氏は、人民銀は貸出金利ベンチマークの改革を推進するため、今後政策指針を示すと述べた。この改革では、融資における最優遇貸出金利（ＬＰＲ）への比較的高い依存度合いを引き下げ、より多様化したベンチマークへの移行を進める。

同氏は、財務体質が良好な一部の企業は金融機関との協議を経て、変動金利融資の基準として銀行間翌日物レポ金利かＬＰＲのいずれかを選択できるようになる可能性があると述べた。

同氏はまた、人民銀は常設貸出ファシリティー（ＳＬＦ）の利用資格を有する金融機関の範囲を拡大し、非銀行系金融機関向けの流動性支援ツールを設ける予定だと述べた。これらの措置は、保険会社やファンド運用会社を含むノンバンク系金融機関への流動性支援を強化することを目的としている。

item.title: 経産省、ラピダスに27年度から3年で4000億円の産業投資計画
item.description:
Kentaro Okasaka
[東京 １９日 ロイター] - 経済産業省は１９日、先端半導体の量産を目指すラピダス...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
経産省、ラピダスに27年度から3年で4000億円の産業投資計画 10/19 19:27 配信

2026年8月21日、都内の本社で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 １９日 ロイター] - 経済産業省は１９日、先端半導体の量産を目指すラピダス（東京都千代田区）向けに、２０２７ー２９年度に産業投資として計４０００億円の出資を要求する計画を明らかにした。財政制度等審議会（財務相の諮問機関）の財政投融資分科会への説明資料で明らかになった。

政府はこれまでに計２５００億円をラピダスに出資しており、今回の産業投資計画が全て実施された場合、累計出資額は６５００億円となる。経産省は、ラピダスが民間融資を受けるためには一定の自己資本比率の維持が必要と指摘。「事業が進捗し、リターンの見通しが相対的に高まっている」とラピダスへの投資意義を説明した。

資料によると、昨年、民間金融機関からラピダスへ２兆円の融資に関する法的拘束力のない意向表明書が発出され、融資実行についての調整・交渉を実施中という。

item.title: Alberta votes to remain part of Canada, CBC News says
item.description: Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation, CBC News said late Monday, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid an ongoing trade war with the US.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Stephenson, Maria Cheng
item.content:encoded: Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on [USN:L6N3Z2101 TEXT:"separation"], CBC News said late Monday, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid an ongoing [USN:SPN44J009 TEXT:"trade war "]with the US. The [USN:L6N46019J TEXT:"referendum"] was nonbinding and asked residents if they wanted to stay part of Canada or start the legal process required to have a binding vote on separation. Pollsters and analysts had repeatedly dismissed the possibility of a separatist victory, citing data that showed about one-third of residents in the Western province supported having a future referendum over leaving the province.

item.title: 製造業中心の日本、攻撃者にとって高価値＝トレンドマイクロＣＥＯ
item.description:
Kentaro Okasaka
[東京 １９日 ロイター] - トレンドマイクロのエバ・チェン社長は１９日、都内で記...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
製造業中心の日本、攻撃者にとって高価値＝トレンドマイクロＣＥＯ 10/19 18:33 配信

2022年9月20日、台湾・台北で撮影されたトレンドマイクロのブース。REUTERS/Ann Wang

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 １９日 ロイター] - トレンドマイクロのエバ・チェン社長は１９日、都内で記者会見し、サイバー攻撃は世界的に増えているものの、日本で特に急増していると述べた。背景として、日本が経済大国で、かつ製造業が基幹産業であること、また企業が正確な記録を整然と保存しているため攻撃者にとって価値が高いことを挙げた。

製造業が狙われる理由としては、生産や製造のプロセスが止まれば大きな被害が出るため「（攻撃者にとっては）より多くの金銭を稼ぐチャンスがある」と述べた。また、日本語という言語の壁がこれまで攻撃を抑制してきたものの「ＡＩ（人工知能）によって壁が消えた」とも指摘した。

チェン氏は、日本が既存のサイバーセキュリティ―インフラに頼り過ぎてきたとの見方も示した。同社の法人向けセキュリティープラットフォーム「トレンドＡＩ　ビジョン・ワン」の採用率は世界で５０％超なのに対し、日本では約２０％にとどまっているとし「日本の顧客、市民の一人一人がもっと警戒心を持って対応する必要がある」と語った。

item.title: POLL Bank Indonesia narrowly expected to hold interest rates despite market turmoil
item.description: Indonesia's central bank will hold interest rates steady on Wednesday, according to a narrow majority of economists in a Reuters poll who said the rupiah's slide following a warning Indonesian stocks might be dropped from key global indexes would have little bearing on the policy decision.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Trivedi
item.content:encoded: Indonesia's central bank will hold interest rates steady on Wednesday, according to a narrow majority of economists in a Reuters poll who said the rupiah's slide following a warning Indonesian stocks might be dropped from key global indexes would have little bearing on the policy decision. The currency, down about 8% so far this year, fell nearly 1% after MSCI shocked domestic markets on Friday when it said it was considering moving Indonesia to "standalone" status from the "emerging markets" designation it has held since 1989. The warning prompted some economists to change their forecasts on Friday and Monday from expectations of no rate change on October 21 to a rate hike. Citibank, which expected no move, now forecasts a pre-emptive 50-basis-point increase. But [USN:L1N45N03U TEXT:"prices"] remain broadly contained. Headline inflation was 3.28% in September, within BI's 1.5% to 3.5% target range, while the core measure eased to 2.84%, which may give policymakers confidence to hold rates for now. Slightly more than half of economists polled (15 of 29) from October 13 to 19, expected Bank Indonesia to keep its benchmark 7-day reverse repurchase rate (IDCBRR=ECI) at 5.75% on Wednesday. They also expected it to leave its overnight deposit and lending facility rates unchanged at 4.75% and 6.50%, respectively. Jakarta's benchmark stock index (.JKSE) , already the world's worst performer this year, [USN:L1N46500W TEXT:"fell"] a further 5% in early trading on Monday, after plunging 11.6% on Friday, its worst one-day fall since January 1998 following MSCI's surprise warning. "I think it's far too early to suggest this will matter from a monetary policy perspective ... but obviously Friday's news has complicated things," said Miguel Chanco, chief emerging Asia economist at UK-based Pantheon Macroeconomics. "Barring (this) event...which is a shock to everyone, the fundamentals still don't suggest to me hiking is necessary, especially after Bank Indonesia already hiked by 100 basis points earlier this year." Some economists argued BI could continue relying on non-rate measures to maintain currency stability, including lowering the cost of foreign-exchange hedging with the central bank, encouraging the use of currencies other than the US dollar, and drawing on its $146.3 billion in FX reserves rather than raising rates. But a comfortable majority of economists, 15 of 22, expected the key rate to rise from 5.75% to 6.00% or more before year-end. That [USN:L4N45D00H TEXT:"view"] was held even before the blow from MSCI, reflecting concerns higher oil prices could lift inflation and a hawkish US Federal Reserve would keep pressure on the rupiah. There was no clear consensus among economists on where borrowing costs would go beyond this year. The median forecast showed the policy rate remaining at 6.00% throughout 2027. "At the end of the day, one of their very clear priorities is IDR stability," said Lavanya Venkateswaran, senior ASEAN economist at OCBC Bank, who brought forward a December rate hike forecast to Wednesday. ([USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"Other stories"] from the Reuters global economic poll)

Shinichi Uchida
［東京 １９日 ロイター］ - 光部品・デバイス事業を手掛ける湖北工業は１９日、東...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
光部品・デバイスの湖北工業、26日付でプライム市場に変更 10/19 17:31 配信

Shinichi Uchida

［東京　１９日　ロイター］ - 光部品・デバイス事業を手掛ける湖北工業は１９日、東証の承認を受け、上場市場区分が２６日付で東証スタンダード市場からプライム市場に変更されると発表した。自動車や産業機器などで使われるアルミ電解コンデンサ用リード端子や、海底ケーブル用光アイソレータで世界シェアトップとされている。

同社株の流通株式比率は６月末で３８．０８％で、プライム市場の上場維持基準（３５％以上）に近い水準にある。今後の状況次第では適合状況に影響を及ぼす可能性もあり、その場合は大株主による株式売り出し、新株発行などの資本政策を含め対応を適切に検討するという。

item.title: ありあけキャピタル、愛媛銀株を大量保有 いよぎんＨＤとの統合控え
item.description:
Mayu Sakoda
[東京 １９日 ロイター] - 投資運用会社のありあけキャピタル（東京都中央区）が愛媛銀行...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ありあけキャピタル、愛媛銀株を大量保有　いよぎんＨＤとの統合控え 10/19 17:08 配信

Mayu Sakoda

[東京 １９日 ロイター] - 投資運用会社のありあけキャピタル（東京都中央区）が愛媛銀行株を５．１９％保有していることが１９日提出の大量保有報告書で分かった。報告義務発生日は９日。

ありあけキャピタルは保有目的として「純投資を基本とする」とし、その上で愛媛銀が基本合意したいよぎんホールディングスとの経営統合について、企業価値向上および株主共同の利益確保の観点から経営陣との対話・助言を行っていると説明している。具体的には統合条件の考え方、船舶ファイナンス事業の集中リスクの管理、成長戦略、資本政策などについて建設的な対話を継続する方針としている。

愛媛銀といよぎんＨＤは２０２６年１２月に最終契約および株式交換契約を締結し、２０２７年２月に愛媛銀の臨時株主総会を開く予定。

item.title: France imposes curfews in parts of Paris, other cities after weekend of riots
item.description: French authorities set curfews in parts of several cities on Monday, including Paris, Lille and Nice, as they faced pressure over security failings after a weekend of riots and looting stemming from anti-government protests.
item.dc:creator: Sudip Kar-Gupta, Elizabeth Pineau
item.content:encoded: French authorities set curfews in parts of several cities on Monday, including Paris, Lille and Nice, as they faced pressure over security failings after a [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"weekend of riots and looting"] stemming from nationwide anti-government protests. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu had ruled out a blanket curfew in Paris but not a state of emergency, and had said it was more appropriate for now to apply partial and localised curfews. "My determination to restore order is absolute," he told reporters. Paris police said they had issued orders barring protests in certain areas of the French capital from 8 p.m. (1800 GMT) and had issued a curfew around the Place de la Republique and Les Halles from 11:00 p.m. Both would remain in effect until 6 a.m. on Tuesday morning. "A police deployment is in place to ensure strict compliance with these measures," the police said in a statement. A source in Lecornu's office said a curfew for minors had been set between 8 p.m. and 6 a.m. for the next two days in Lille, Douai, Wattignies and Denain with the agreement of the local mayors. In Nice, mayor Eric Ciotti said in a video posted online that he had signed an order installing a curfew for minors in central Nice overnight. Marseille banned gatherings and demonstrations. French unions meanwhile called for a new round of strikes and rallies on November 5. The [USN:L1N4650EF TEXT:"weekend of looting"] and violence between some protesters and police followed weeks of student demonstrations, rocking France six months ahead of its [USN:L6N4650JF TEXT:"next presidential election"] and highlighting pressures from a weak economy and surging debt. MINISTER BLAMES FAR LEFT Lecornu blamed far-left groups for some of France's worst unrest in years. "There is, after all, a far-left movement that wants to cause — we can’t put it any more strongly — profound unrest in the country in the run-up to the presidential election," he said. Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon urged him to provide evidence. "Otherwise, he should apologise, keep quiet and stop fanning the flames of unrest," he said on X. The Federation of Trade and Retail said almost 3,000 shops had been affected over the weekend. "Behind every ransacked shop are business owners, employees and families who have seen years of work and effort wiped out in a matter of hours," it added, calling for social security and tax relief for affected businesses. Lecornu said the government would provide furlough measures from Tuesday. Standing before a boarded-up shopfront, Gerard Nouchi, manager of two clothing stores in Marseille, said there weren't enough police to stop the looters. "They trashed everything, broke things, insulted us,” Nouchi said. "It was like a real tornado." The government ordered platforms selling looted goods to take down announcements and collaborate to prosecute resellers, Junior Digital Minister Anne Le Hénanff wrote on X. Some 2,400 people were arrested and one protester died from a cardiac arrest on Saturday while nearly 1,000 officers were injured, according to the Interior Ministry. 'LEFT WITHOUT PROTECTION' French assets [USN:L1N46507D TEXT:"were underperforming"] broader European markets on Monday, though moves were more contained than at some other moments of recent political friction. Tensions in President Emmanuel Macron's fragile government over apparent security shortcomings — coming as the government needs to pass a budget bill to rein in its finances — could further [USN:L8N46508Y TEXT:"unsettle investors"]. Macron's office said on Monday he had turned down his Interior Minister Laurent Nunez's offer to resign, telling him instead to put an end to barricades and looting and be transparent over what Macron called "intelligence and foresight failings". Nunez told reporters that Tuesday evening's Champions League soccer match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona would go ahead as planned. The mayors of Paris, Marseille and Lyon said in a joint op-ed in the newspaper Liberation that they were used to demonstrations and protests. "But on Saturday ... for the first time, we had the feeling that whole sections of our cities had been left without protection," said the mayors, all from the centre-left. The start of school holidays on Monday may provide relief, but students were staging more gatherings and blockades in some places, including the Louvre gallery and Sciences Po university in central Paris. LUXURY BOUTIQUES DAMAGED At the weekend, hundreds of thousands took to the streets to protest over what many say are declining and dysfunctional public services. At the Place Vendome in Paris, home to luxury hotels and boutiques, most shops were shuttered and surrounded by security guards on Monday. The front door of a Dior boutique was smashed, while windows belonging to other luxury brand stores in central Paris, including Rolex, Louis Vuitton, Ralph Lauren and Gucci, were damaged. In Marseille, Ligue 1 club [USN:L4N4650P2 TEXT:"Olympique de Marseille"] said its official store on the city's historic main avenue had been looted, while a town hall in central France [USN:L1N46402C TEXT:"was torched"]. France deployed 60,000 police and other security forces on Saturday, Nunez told France Inter radio, but he acknowledged that was not enough to control violent crowds. Cost-of-living issues also drove weekend protests in other European countries including [USN:L8N463090 TEXT:"Italy"], [USN:L6N46303L TEXT:"Belgium"] and [USN:L6N4620YF TEXT:"Albania"]. European governments [USN:L8N4650JR TEXT:"have advised"] citizens travelling to France to avoid large crowds and exercise caution. As France was busy cleaning up its streets, Macron arrived in Kuwait for a Gulf trip aimed at securing additional petrol and diesel supplies to bring down pump prices.

item.title: Zelenskiy says Ukraine got no warning as Russian missiles rain in
item.description: Ukraine received no advance warning from its partners of a Russian ballistic missile strike overnight, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, adding that some vital deliveries from the United States were being delayed.
item.dc:creator: Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Ukraine received no advance warning from its partners of a Russian ballistic missile strike overnight, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, adding that some vital deliveries from the United States were being delayed. Moscow launched one of its broadest air assaults in months overnight, cutting power to more than half a million households and damaging energy infrastructure across Ukraine. Ten people were reported killed. A Russian drone attack killed six people, including two children, in a park near Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, according to the regional governor, Oleh Syniehubov. Zelenskiy called the strike "an act of absolute barbarity". In all, Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles overnight at Kyiv and the surrounding region and more than 200 drones in attacks stretching from Kharkiv and Dnipro in the east to Odesa in the south and Volyn and Rivne in the west. Two people were killed in Kyiv and the nearby region and two more in the industrial city of Kryvyi Rih, officials said. HIGH TENSIONS Tensions are running high between Zelenskiy and President Donald Trump's administration over US support for Ukraine and Washington's approach to Russia. "Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners," Zelenskiy said on the Telegram app. "When deliveries of missiles for Ukraine's air defence are blocked while Russia is granted relief or delays in sanctions, this is, unfortunately, a denial of reality on the part of our partners." Zelenskiy later said he had [USN:L4N4651DO TEXT:"discussed"] speeding up supplies of the Patriot system, vital to countering Russian ballistic missiles, with representatives of the US company Lockheed Martin. "It is their Patriot systems and F-16 planes that play an important role in defending against Russian ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones. The company is now boosting production of ballistic interceptors. We are hoping that we will be able to buy some of them to protect more lives," Zelenskiy said on Telegram. "And things are not easy on both fronts right now. We talked about how we can expand and increase supplies." For several months, Ukraine has suffered from critical shortages of US-made Patriot missiles. Zelenskiy said earlier that the United States had slowed some vital supplies for Ukraine, adding that the delays were at the US Defense Department level. He provided no other details. Kyiv has previously said it has struggled to get interceptors critical to repelling Russian missile attacks. Zelenskiy said that some political agreements on air defence were not implemented at a working level. Throughout the nearly five-year war, Ukraine has relied on US intelligence to detect Russian ballistic missile launches and provide early warning of incoming strikes. Yurii Ihnat, a spokesman for the Ukrainian air force, said Kyiv received no warning ahead of the first ballistic missile strike overnight but did receive information ahead of a second attack. "For some reason, no information was received the first time, a matter our experts are investigating together with our partners, as this is not the first time such a situation has occurred," Ihnat told Ukrainian television. Secretary of State Marco Rubio [USN:L1N465065 TEXT:"denied"] that the United States had paused some intelligence sharing with Ukraine. Ukrainian air defences downed 247 targets - four cruise missiles and 243 drones, the air force said. Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces carried out a "massive strike" using precision weapons and attack drones against Ukrainian defence industry facilities, drone and cruise missile storage sites, and a data centre. Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said the energy sector was the main target of the attacks, with damage reported across the country. Ukraine's energy ministry said rolling blackouts were introduced for households and businesses as crews worked to restore supplies. Koretskyi said Russia has hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure more than 2,000 times since mid-July, intensifying its attacks from previous years of the war.

item.title: Antofagasta’s Centinela strike ends after deal with unions
item.description: Workers from two unions at Chile’s Centinela copper mine have ratified an agreement reached with Antofagasta Minerals on a new collective bargaining contra
item.dc:creator: Mining.com
item.content:encoded: Workers from two unions at Chile’s Centinela copper mine have ratified an agreement reached with Antofagasta Minerals on a new collective bargaining contract, ending a strike of more than a week, the unions and the company said on Sunday. More than 700 members of the Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions began the strike on October 7 after contract talks broke down. They had sought equal benefits for workers regardless of which union they belonged to. The parties returned to the negotiating table on Tuesday in an effort to resolve the dispute. “The Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions announce the successful conclusion of our collective bargaining process, after 94.49% of participating workers voted to approve the proposed collective agreement,” the unions said in a statement, which was followed by a company statement confirming the deal. Three workers had been on a hunger strike in an effort to pressure both sides into finding a solution to the deadlocked talks. Antofagasta said on Wednesday it had managed to maintain production at normal levels, avoiding any negative impact from the strike at the mine, which produced 240,400 metric tons of copper in 2025. The strike at Centinela, along with the ultimately unrealized risk of a supervisors’ strike at BHP’s Escondida mine, had been supporting global copper prices amid concerns about the industry’s ability to increase supply sufficiently to meet expected future demand. (Reporting by Fabian Cambero; Editing by William Mallard)

item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: Nasdaq et S&P 500 en hausse avec le rebond des valeurs liées à l'IA
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nasdaq et S&P 500 en hausse avec le rebond des valeurs liées à l'IA 19 octobre (Reuters) - Le Nasdaq et le S&P 500 ont rebondi lundi à Wall Street portés par le rebond des valeurs liées à l'intelligence artificielle après le fort mouvement de vente de la semaine dernière, tandis que le recul des cours du pétrole a également soutenu la tendance avant une série de résultats d'entreprises très attendus. L'Europe finit dans le rouge, pénalisée par les tensions après les événements en France 19 octobre (Reuters) - Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en nette baisse lundi, face aux craintes d'instabilité politique et financière en France à la suite des scènes de chaos en marge de la mobilisation nationale de samedi contre la vie chère. Solvay abaisse ses objectifs annuels, le conflit au Moyen-Orient pèse 19 octobre (Reuters) - Solvay a abaissé lundi ses objectifs pour l'ensemble de l'année 2026, le groupe chimique belge prenant acte du fait que le conflit au Moyen-Orient et l'arrêt d'une usine de peroxyde en Arabie saoudite ont pesé sur ses résultats du seul troisième trimestre. Indonésie: La sécheresse provoquée par El Niño pèse sur les producteurs d’huile de palme SANGGAU, Indonésie/DJAKARTA, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Après quatre jours d'attente devant une huilerie du Kalimantan occidental, dans la partie indonésienne de Bornéo, Supendi a dû repartir avec sa récolte de fruits de palmier sur les bras, l'usine n'étant plus en mesure d'accepter de nouveaux chargements. Orange et trois opérateurs envisagent une candidature conjointe pour l'attribution de fréquences MSS FRANCFORT, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Orange, Deutsche Telekom, Telefonica et Vodafone ont annoncé lundi étudier la possibilité de présenter une offre conjointe en vue de la future attribution de fréquences pour les services mobiles par satellite (MSS) en Europe. Carrefour conclut un accord pour racheter Codifrance à Colruyt 19 octobre (Reuters) - Carrefour a annoncé lundi avoir conclu un accord avec le groupe belge Colruyt pour l’acquisition de Codifrance, spécialisé dans l’affiliation et de la distribution alimentaire de proximité, pour une valeur d'entreprise de 152 millions d'euros. Alstom remporte une commande d'environ €800 mlns au Vietnam 19 octobre (Reuters) - Alstom a annoncé lundi avoir remporté une première commande d'environ 800 millions d'euros au Vietnam pour la fourniture de trains Metropolis, à la suite d'un accord signé entre le groupe français et Vingroup. Chine-La croissance économique a accéléré plus qu'attendu au troisième trimestre L'économie chinoise a accéléré au troisième trimestre à un rythme supérieur aux attentes, alors que la solidité des exportations et de l'activité manufacturière a compensé la morosité prolongée de la demande intérieure, atténuant la pression sur Pékin pour le déploiement de nouvelles mesures de stimulus afin d'atteindre l'objectif annuel de croissance. Shell s’accorde avec DCC Energy sur la cession de ses stations-service en France, selon une source Shell a scellé une entente avec DCC Energy, basée à Dublin, pour la vente de son réseau de stations-service et de services connexes en France, selon une source proche du dossier et des documents consultés par Reuters. UniCredit autorisé par la BCE à prendre le contrôle de Commerzbank UniCredit a obtenu l'autorisation de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) pour prendre le contrôle de Commerzbank, a annoncé jeudi soir la banque italienne, alors que son offre publique d'achat hostile a porté sa participation dans son concurrent allemand à 48%.

item.title: OFRMO Summary
item.description: Trump juge que Kyiv devrait écarter Zelensky des négociations
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Trump juge que Kyiv devrait écarter Zelensky des négociations 19 octobre (Reuters) - Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré lundi qu'il estimait qu'une autre personne que le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky devrait négocier au nom de Kyiv dans le cadre des efforts visant à mettre fin à la guerre avec la Russie. Yémen-Cinquante-trois morts dans une attaque houthie contre un camp militaire gouvernemental 19 octobre (Reuters) - Cinquante-trois personnes ont été tuées lundi et 200 blessées dans une attaque des rebelles houthis, soutenus par l'Iran, contre un camp d'entraînement militaire du gouvernement yéménite dans la province de Chabwa, dans l'est du Yémen, selon des responsables gouvernementaux. Italie-Les boutiques de Milan ont fermé plus tôt, craintes de nouveaux pillages MILAN, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Les magasins du centre de Milan ont fermé plus tôt que d'habitude lundi et ont barricadé leurs vitrines, craignant de nouveaux troubles après deux jours de manifestations au cours desquels des groupes de personnes cagoulées se sont affrontés avec la police, ont pillé des magasins et saccagé des biens. Grèce: Douze migrants, dont un nourrisson, se noient dans deux naufrages au large des îles grecques 19 octobre (Reuters) - Douze migrants, dont un nourrisson, se sont noyés lundi lors de deux accidents différents au large des îles grecques de Lesbos et de Samos, dans le nord-est de la mer Égée, après le chavirement de leurs embarcations alors qu'elles étaient poursuivies par les garde-côtes, ont indiqué les autorités. Australie-Une députée dans un état critique après avoir été percutée délibérement par une voiture SYDNEY, 19 octobre (Reuters) - La députée australienne Helen Haines est dans un état critique après avoir été délibérément percutée lundi par une voiture devant son bureau, à Wangaratta, au nord-est de Melbourne. Gaza-Faute de fonds, le PAM réduit son aide à 500.000 Palestiniens LE CAIRE/GAZA, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM) des Nations Unies a déclaré lundi que le manque de financement l'obligeait à réduire considérablement son programme d'aide à Gaza, laissant ainsi environ 500.000 personnes sans aide alimentaire mensuelle sur un territoire où les deux tiers de la population restent en situation d'insécurité alimentaire aiguë. La police israélienne arrête 10 personnes en lien avec les diplomates européens attaqués par des colons en Cisjordanie occupée TEl AVIV , 19 octobre (Reuters) - La police israélienne a annoncé lundi avoir arrêté dix suspects dans le cadre de son enquête sur les incidents violents survenus ce week-end en Cisjordanie occupée, notamment des agressions menées par des colons juifs à la fois contre des diplomates européens et une journaliste du Washington Post. France-Lecornu demande des couvre-feux partiels à la suite des violences PARIS, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Le Premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, a annoncé qu'il demandait l'instauration dès ce lundi de couvre-feux localisés et partiels en France à la suite des violences et des pillages en marge de manifestations samedi où se mêlaient revendications des lycéens et mécontentement face au coût de la vie. Brésil-Premier débat entre Bolsonaro et Lula, les attaques personnelles fusent Le sénateur Flavio Bolsonaro et le président sortant Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, qui s'affronteront lors du second tour de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil le 25 octobre, ont participé dimanche soir à un premier débat télévisé tendu lors duquel les attaques personnelles ont fusé. L'Ukraine pas avertie de nouvelles frappes russes, qui ont fait quatre morts - Zelensky La Russie a de nouveau frappé Kyiv et ses environs sans que l'Ukraine n'ait été avertie au préalable, a déclaré le président du pays Volodimir Zelensky, qui a également fait état d'un retard de livraisons d'équipements essentiels en provenance des Etats-Unis.

item.title: OFRTP Summary
item.description: France: Vinted retire de la vente les articles soupçonnés d'être volés en marge des manifestations
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France: Vinted retire de la vente les articles soupçonnés d'être volés en marge des manifestations 19 octobre (Reuters) - L'application dédiée à l'achat et à la vente de vêtements d'occasion Vinted a annoncé lundi avoir renforcé les contrôles sur les annonces suspectes et supprimé celles revendant des biens pillés en marge des manifestations de ce weekend en France. Macron dit vouloir punir les "casseurs" et écouter les manifestants Emmanuel Macron a fait dimanche la distinction entre les "casseurs" et les manifestants aux "revendications légitimes", invitant le gouvernement à faire en sorte que le chaos constaté la veille "ne puisse pas se reproduire". Suède: La dirigeante du Parti du Centre va étudier la possibilité de former un gouvernement STOCKHOLM, 19 octobre (Reuters) - Le président du Parlement suédois a déclaré lundi avoir demandé à la dirigeante du Parti du Centre, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, d'étudier les possibilités de formation d'un nouveau gouvernement, lui accordant une semaine pour rencontrer les autres partis. 855 interpellations samedi à Paris, décès d'un manifestant d'un arrêt cardiorespiratoire - préfecture Un manifestant est décédé à la suite d'un arrêt cardiorespiratoire samedi à Paris lors des manifestations contre la vie chère, pendant lesquelles 855 interpellations ont été effectuées, ce qui représente un "chiffre record", a déclaré dimanche la préfecture de police. Paris condamne l'agression d'un maire français par des colons juifs La France a condamné dimanche l'agression "gravissime" par des colons juifs du maire d'Aulnoye-Aymeries survenue la veille dans le village palestinien de Taybeh. France et Allemagne d'accord sur un plan pour l'automobile La France et l'Allemagne ont annoncé vendredi un accord sur une "approche commune" visant à garantir l'avenir de l'industrie automobile européenne, avec un accent mis à la fois sur la transition énergétique et sur une production des véhicules en Europe. Les tortues caouannes, sentinelles du réchauffement en Méditerranée Sous un ciel baigné de lune, des bébés tortues sortent du sable sur la côte méditerranéenne turque et se hâtent vers la mer, dans un cycle naturel ancestral de plus en plus menacé par le changement climatique. Une étoile verte récemment découverte émerveille les astronomes Pour la première fois, des astronomes ont identifié une étoile verte, un vestige stellaire dense appelé "naine blanche", qui a pris une teinte fantomatique de vert chartreuse après avoir absorbé des débris rocheux provenant de planètes qui, autrefois, gravitaient autour d’elle. La santé du pape Léon en "amélioration constante", dit le Vatican Le pape Léon XIV continue de se remettre de son intervention chirurgicale subie mardi pour un nodule cancéreux au poumon, a déclaré vendredi le Vatican, soulignant "l'amélioration constante" de son état de santé. Le pape Léon XIV se rétablit comme prévu de son opération d'un cancer du poumon Le rétablissement du pape Léon XIV de son opération d'un cancer du poumon suit son cours, a annoncé jeudi le Vatican, qui précise que le souverain pontife de 71 ans a recommencé à travailler.
